title: Golden Section play frontmatter
description: The frontmatter contract for a file in plays/<category>/. Enforced by scripts/build.mjs, which also checks constraints this schema cannot express: that slug equals the filename, that category matches the containing folder, that slug/anchor/order are unique across all plays, that every preventsMistakes number exists in MISTAKES.md, and that every referenced template file is present in templates/.

order.description: Position in the overall play sequence. Unique across all plays.

slug.description: URL segment and filename stem. Changing it breaks existing links — treat as permanent.

anchor.description: Stable cross-reference id, used by the website's master page. Treat as permanent.

title.description: Short label, used in indexes, tables, and generated link text.

h1.description: Headline for the play's own page. Usually phrased as 'How to …'.

players.description: Who runs this play, as a comma-separated list of roles.

initialEffort.description: Effort to stand the play up the first time, in story points, e.g. '21 SP'. A point is one person's working time; see EFFORT.md for the scale. An em dash where effort is not meaningfully bounded.

ongoingEffort.description: Effort for ONE recurrence at the play's cadence, in story points, not the annual total; see EFFORT.md. An em dash where not applicable.

stage.description: The earliest company stage at which this play starts paying for itself.

summary.description: One paragraph that answers the question directly. Used as the bolded lead everywhere the play appears.

questions.description: Questions this play answers, phrased as a founder would ask them.

preventsMistakes.description: Mistake numbers from MISTAKES.md. This is the ONLY place the play-to-mistake relationship is declared; every link in the other direction is generated from it. May be empty for a play that prevents no catalogued mistake.

templates.description: Downloadable templates belonging to this play. Optional.

file.description: Filename inside templates/, keeping its binder number.

name.description: Display name for the download link.

format.description: Set to 'html' only where the body needs structure the Markdown dialect cannot express, such as headings inside list items. One play currently uses this.
